qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest dipole moment?

text_solutions: Dipole moment depends on electronegativity difference and bond length. \( \ce{CH3F} \) has the highest dipole moment due to fluorine’s high electronegativity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an aryl halide?

text_solutions: An aryl halide has the halogen directly attached to an aromatic ring. \( \ce{C6H5Br} \) (bromobenzene) is an aryl halide.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) (2-butene) as the major product per Zaitsev’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which halide is a vicinal dihalide?

text_solutions: A vicinal dihalide has halogens on adjacent carbons. \( \ce{CH3CHBrCH2Br} \) (1,2-dibromopropane) is a vicinal dihalide.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{HI} \) in the presence of red phosphorus?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HI} \) with red phosphorus converts 1-butanol to 1-iodobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2I} \)) via substitution.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) in sunlight?

text_solutions: Chlorination of pentane favors the secondary position (C2/C4) due to stability, forming \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH2CH3} \) (2-chloropentane) as the major product.

qns_content.text: Which compound has the IUPAC name 3-chloro-2-methylpentane?

text_solutions: 3-Chloro-2-methylpentane is a five-carbon chain (pentane) with Cl on C3 and a methyl group on C2: \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CHClCH2CH3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaI} \) in acetone?

text_solutions: This is a Finkelstein reaction, where \( \ce{NaI} \) in acetone substitutes Cl in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) (1-iodopropane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzene reacts with \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \)?

text_solutions: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \) forms \( \ce{C6H5CH(CH3)2} \) (isopropylbenzene or cumene).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(Cl)CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a four-carbon chain with chlorine on the second carbon. The parent chain is butane, so the name is 2-chlorobutane.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a tertiary halide?

text_solutions: A tertiary halide has the halogen on a carbon bonded to three other carbons. \( \ce{CH3CH2C(CH3)2Cl} \) (2-chloro-2-methylbutane) is tertiary.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a four-carbon chain with chlorine on the first carbon. The parent chain is butane, so the name is 1-chlorobutane.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{HI} \) in the absence of peroxides?

text_solutions: For 2-pentene (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \)), \( \ce{HI} \) adds via Markovnikov’s rule, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CHICH2CH3} \) (3-iodopentane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when chlorobenzene reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \)?

text_solutions: Chlorobenzene undergoes electrophilic substitution with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \), forming 1,4-dichlorobenzene (\( \ce{C6H4Cl2} \)) as the major product (para).

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{HCl} \)?

text_solutions: For 2-pentene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \)), \( \ce{HCl} \) adds via Markovnikov’s rule, forming \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH2CH3} \) (2-chloropentane).

qns_content.text: What is the order of reactivity of alcohols with \( \ce{HBr} \)?

text_solutions: The reactivity of alcohols with haloacids increases with the degree of substitution due to carbocation stability: tertiary > secondary > primary.

qns_content.text: How many dichloro isomers are possible for propane on free radical chlorination?

text_solutions: Propane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \)) can form 1,1-dichloropropane, 1,2-dichloropropane, 1,3-dichloropropane, and 2,2-dichloropropane, totaling 4 isomers.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{KOH} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \), forming \( \ce{CH2=CH2} \) (ethene).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCl} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCl} \), forming \( \ce{CH2=CHCH3} \) (propene).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(Br)CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a five-carbon chain (pentane) with bromine on the third carbon. The name is 3-bromopentane.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a primary halide?

text_solutions: A primary halide has the halogen on a carbon bonded to one other carbon. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromobutane) is primary.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a five-carbon chain (pentane) with chlorine on the fourth carbon. The name is 4-chloropentane.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts ethanol to ethyl bromide with \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Ethanol reacts with \( \ce{NaBr} \) and \( \ce{H2SO4} \) to form ethyl bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \)) via nucleophilic substitution, with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) aiding dehydration.

qns_content.text: Which reagent reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2OH} \) to produce \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2Br} \) and a phosphorus-containing byproduct?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PBr3} \) converts 1-pentanol to 1-bromopentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2Br} \)) with \( \ce{H3PO3} \) as a byproduct.

qns_content.text: Which nucleophile converts \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OC(CH3)3} \) in a polar aprotic solvent?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaOC(CH3)3} \) (sodium tert-butoxide) substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OC(CH3)3} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in ether to produce \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) as the major product?

text_solutions: Wurtz reaction couples two \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) (1-chloropropane) molecules with \( \ce{Na} \) to form pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: How many monobromo isomers are possible for \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylbutane has four unique carbon positions for Br substitution (C1, C2 with methyl, C3, C4), yielding 4 isomers.

qns_content.text: Which halide is formed when benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution with chlorine in the presence of a Lewis acid?

text_solutions: Electrophilic substitution of benzene with chlorine and a Lewis acid (e.g., \( \ce{FeCl3} \)) replaces a hydrogen with chlorine, forming chlorobenzene (\( \ce{C6H5Cl} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaCN} \) in DMSO?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaCN} \) in DMSO (polar aprotic solvent) substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CN} \) (butanenitrile).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a four-carbon chain with a chlorine atom on the second carbon. The parent chain is butane, and the chlorine is a substituent, so the name is 2-chlorobutane.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHBrCH3} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHBrCH3} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \) (2-pentene) per Zaitsev’s rule.

qns_content.text: What is the order of reactivity of halogens in free radical halogenation of alkanes?

text_solutions: Reactivity in free radical halogenation decreases with bond strength: \( \ce{F2} \) > \( \ce{Cl2} \) > \( \ce{Br2} \) > \( \ce{I2} \).

qns_content.text: Which alkane produces \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \) as the major product on chlorination in sunlight?

text_solutions: Pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) on chlorination favors the secondary position (C3), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \) (3-chloropentane).

qns_content.text: Which nucleophile replaces Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2ONO2} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{AgNO3} \) provides \( \ce{NO3^-} \), which substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) to form the nitrate ester \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2ONO2} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the lowest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling point decreases with lower molecular weight. \( \ce{CH3CH2F} \) has the lowest molecular weight among the options.

qns_content.text: What is the precipitate formed when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts via \( \ce{S_N1} \) with \( \ce{AgNO3} \), forming \( \ce{AgBr} \) (yellow precipitate) and \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2ONO2} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaSH} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaSH} \) provides \( \ce{SH^-} \), which substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2SH} \) (ethanethiol).

qns_content.text: What is the leaving group in the reaction of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) with \( \ce{KCN} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CN} \)?

text_solutions: In the \( \ce{S_N2} \) reaction, \( \ce{Br^-} \) is displaced by \( \ce{CN^-} \) and acts as the leaving group.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a primary alkyl halide?

text_solutions: A primary alkyl halide has the halogen attached to a carbon bonded to only one other carbon. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromopropane) fits this definition.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CHClCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{Mg} \) in dry ether, followed by \( \ce{H2O} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CHClCH3} \) forms a Grignard reagent (\( \ce{CH3CH(MgCl)CH3} \)) with \( \ce{Mg} \), which hydrolyzes with \( \ce{H2O} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \) (propane).

qns_content.text: Which halide on reaction with \( \ce{KOH} \) in water forms \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \) substitutes Cl in \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH2CH3} \) (2-chloropentane) via \( \ce{S_N2} \) to form 2-pentanol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a secondary alkyl halide?

text_solutions: A secondary alkyl halide has the halogen on a carbon bonded to two other carbons. \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH3} \) (2-chlorobutane) is secondary.

qns_content.text: How many monobromo derivatives are possible for \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Butane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)) has two types of hydrogens: 6 primary (terminal) and 4 secondary (middle). Bromination gives 1-bromobutane and 2-bromobutane, so 2 isomers.

qns_content.text: How many structural isomers are possible for \( \ce{C4H9Cl} \)?

text_solutions: For \( \ce{C4H9Cl} \), the isomers are 1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane, totaling 4.

qns_content.text: Which of the following undergoes \( \ce{S_N2} \) substitution most readily?

text_solutions: \( \ce{S_N2} \) favors primary halides due to less steric hindrance. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) (1-chloropropane) is most reactive among the options.

qns_content.text: Which reaction produces a mixture of 1-chloropropane and 2-chloropropane?

text_solutions: Free radical chlorination of propane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \)) with \( \ce{Cl2} \) in light substitutes Cl at C1 or C2, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{CH3CHClCH3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{PBr3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PBr3} \) converts ethanol to ethyl bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \)) by replacing the \( \ce{OH} \) group with Br.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when benzene reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) in sunlight?

text_solutions: In sunlight, \( \ce{Cl2} \) adds to benzene via free radical mechanism, forming \( \ce{C6H6Cl6} \) (hexachlorocyclohexane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{NH3} \) (excess)?

text_solutions: Excess \( \ce{NH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) via nucleophilic substitution to form the primary amine \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \) (propylamine).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a benzylic halide?

text_solutions: A benzylic halide has the halogen on a carbon directly attached to a benzene ring. \( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \) (benzyl chloride) fits this definition.

qns_content.text: What is the byproduct when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaI} \) in acetone to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \)?

text_solutions: In the Finkelstein reaction, \( \ce{NaI} \) displaces Cl, forming \( \ce{NaCl} \) as a precipitate byproduct.

qns_content.text: What is the order of reactivity of alkyl halides with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol tests \( \ce{S_N1} \) reactivity, which depends on carbocation stability: tertiary > secondary > primary.

qns_content.text: Which halide produces a tertiary alcohol when reacted with \( \ce{KOH} \) in water?

text_solutions: \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2C(CH3)2Cl} \) undergoes \( \ce{S_N1} \) with \( \ce{KOH} \) in water, forming \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2C(CH3)2OH} \), a tertiary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts 2-methyl-2-propanol to 2-chloro-2-methylpropane?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HCl} \) reacts with 2-methyl-2-propanol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)) to form 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (\( \ce{(CH3)3CCl} \)) via \( \ce{S_N1} \) substitution.

qns_content.text: How many monochloro isomers are possible for \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylbutane has four distinct carbon positions for Cl substitution: C1, C2 (with methyl), C3, and C4, yielding 4 isomers.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{AgF} \)?

text_solutions: The Swarts reaction with \( \ce{AgF} \) substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2F} \) (1-fluoropropane).

qns_content.text: Which halide undergoes elimination most readily with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Tertiary halides favor elimination (E2) due to steric hindrance and stable alkene formation. \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH2C(CH3)2Br} \) reacts most readily.

qns_content.text: What is the bond angle around the carbon attached to chlorine in \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \), the carbon attached to Cl is tetrahedral (sp³ hybridized), with a bond angle of approximately 109.5°.

qns_content.text: What is the order of dipole moments of \( \ce{CH3F} \), \( \ce{CH3Cl} \), \( \ce{CH3Br} \), and \( \ce{CH3I} \)?

text_solutions: Dipole moment decreases with lower electronegativity difference: \( \ce{CH3F} \) > \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) > \( \ce{CH3Br} \) > \( \ce{CH3I} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide is most reactive towards \( \ce{S_N2} \) substitution?

text_solutions: \( \ce{S_N2} \) reactivity is highest for primary halides due to less steric hindrance. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) (primary iodide) is most reactive.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{KNO2} \) in DMF?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KNO2} \) substitutes Cl via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2ONO} \) (propyl nitrite), as \( \ce{NO2^-} \) bonds through oxygen.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest C-X bond length?

text_solutions: Bond length increases with the size of the halogen. Among F, Cl, Br, and I, iodine is the largest, so \( \ce{CH3-I} \) has the longest C-X bond.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{PCl5} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PCl5} \) converts 1-propanol to 1-chloropropane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \)) by replacing \( \ce{OH} \) with Cl.

qns_content.text: Which halide is an allylic halide?

text_solutions: An allylic halide has the halogen on a carbon adjacent to a double bond. \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2Cl} \) (4-chloro-2-butene) is allylic.

qns_content.text: What is the major alkene formed by dehydrohalogenation of \( \ce{CH3CH(Br)CH3} \) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromopropane with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) follows Zaitsev’s rule, forming the more substituted alkene, \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) (propene).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol to form a precipitate due to allylic stabilization?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2Cl} \) (allyl chloride) forms a stable allylic carbocation via \( \ce{S_N1} \), reacting with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form \( \ce{AgCl} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in the presence of \( \ce{CH3Cl} \)?

text_solutions: This is a Wurtz reaction variant. \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) couple with \( \ce{Na} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \) (propane) as one product.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaOCH3} \) in methanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaOCH3} \) in methanol substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2OCH3} \) (ethyl methyl ether).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a secondary halide?

text_solutions: A secondary halide has the halogen on a carbon bonded to two other carbons. \( \ce{CH3CH2CHBrCH3} \) (3-bromobutane) is secondary.

qns_content.text: Which halide is a benzylic halide?

text_solutions: A benzylic halide has the halogen on a carbon directly attached to a benzene ring. \( \ce{C6H5CH(CH3)Cl} \) (1-chloroethylbenzene) is benzylic.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{HBr} \) in the presence of peroxides?

text_solutions: In the presence of peroxides, \( \ce{HBr} \) adds to propene anti-Markovnikov, with Br attaching to the less substituted carbon, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \).

qns_content.text: Which condition favors the formation of \( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2CH3} \) from benzene and a haloalkane?

text_solutions: Friedel-Crafts alkylation with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \) in anhydrous conditions forms \( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2CH3} \) (propylbenzene).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts slowest with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) to form an alkene?

text_solutions: Primary halides undergo elimination (E2) slowest due to less stable transition states. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts slowest among the options.

qns_content.text: Which of the following forms a white precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) slowest?

text_solutions: Primary halides react slowest with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) via \( \ce{S_N1} \). \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) is primary and forms \( \ce{AgCl} \) slowest among the options.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is prepared by reacting an alkane with \( \ce{Br2} \) in the presence of light?

text_solutions: Free radical bromination of butane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)) with \( \ce{Br2} \) in light forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CHBrCH3} \) (2-bromobutane) as one product.

qns_content.text: Which halide is classified as a secondary benzylic halide?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C6H5CHClCH3} \) (1-chloro-1-phenylethane) has Cl on a carbon attached to a benzene ring (benzylic) and two carbons (secondary).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \) provides \( \ce{OH^-} \), which substitutes Cl in the primary alkyl halide \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \) (1-propanol).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2Br} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2Br} \), forming \( \ce{(CH3)2C=CH2} \) (2-methylpropene).

qns_content.text: What gas is evolved when \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \) in the presence of pyridine to form \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SOCl2} \) with pyridine converts ethanol to ethyl chloride, releasing \( \ce{SO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \) gases; \( \ce{SO2} \) is the key gaseous byproduct.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2I} \) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in dry ether?

text_solutions: This is a Wurtz reaction, coupling two \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2I} \) molecules to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) (octane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaNH2} \) in liquid ammonia?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaNH2} \) (strong base) promotes E2 elimination in \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \) (2-pentene) per Zaitsev’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which alkene reacts with \( \ce{HCl} \) to form a halide that gives \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \) on elimination?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) (2-butene) with \( \ce{HCl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH3} \), which eliminates \( \ce{HCl} \) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) to form 1-butene (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in UV light at 300°C?

text_solutions: Bromination of butane at high temperature favors the more stable secondary radical, forming \( \ce{CH3CHBrCH2CH3} \) (2-bromobutane) as the major product.

qns_content.text: Which of the following gives a yellow precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: Alkyl iodides like \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) react with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form \( \ce{AgI} \), a yellow precipitate, due to easy ionization.

qns_content.text: Which halide yields \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH2CH3} \) as the major product with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) at 80°C?

text_solutions: Elimination (E2) of \( \ce{CH3CH2CHBrCH2CH2CH3} \) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH2CH3} \) (3-hexene) per Zaitsev’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which halide forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) when treated with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) at high temperature?

text_solutions: Elimination (E2) of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromopentane) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) forms 1-pentene (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \)).

qns_content.text: How many chlorine atoms are present in the product when benzene reacts with excess \( \ce{Cl2} \) in sunlight?

text_solutions: Benzene (\( \ce{C6H6} \)) with excess \( \ce{Cl2} \) in sunlight forms hexachlorocyclohexane (\( \ce{C6H6Cl6} \)), which has 6 chlorine atoms.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when aniline reacts with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \), followed by \( \ce{KI} \)?

text_solutions: Aniline forms a diazonium salt with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \), which reacts with \( \ce{KI} \) to form \( \ce{C6H5I} \) (iodobenzene).

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling point increases with molecular weight due to stronger London forces. \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) has the highest molecular weight among the options.

qns_content.text: Which halide is most reactive with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) to form an alkene?

text_solutions: Elimination (E2) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) favors tertiary halides due to stable alkene formation. \( \ce{(CH3)3CBr} \) reacts fastest.

qns_content.text: Which compound corresponds to the IUPAC name 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane?

text_solutions: 1-Bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane is a three-carbon chain (propane) with two methyl groups on C2 and Br on C1: \( \ce{CH2BrC(CH3)2CH3} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol slowest due to its stable C-X bond?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C6H5Cl} \) (chlorobenzene) has a strong C-Cl bond due to sp² hybridization and resonance, making it unreactive in \( \ce{S_N1} \) with \( \ce{AgNO3} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the lowest C-X bond enthalpy?

text_solutions: Bond enthalpy decreases as the halogen size increases due to weaker overlap. \( \ce{CH3-I} \) has the weakest C-X bond among F, Cl, Br, and I.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaOCH3} \) in methanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaOCH3} \) substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OCH3} \) (methyl propyl ether).

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest C-X bond enthalpy?

text_solutions: Bond enthalpy increases with smaller halogen size due to stronger overlap. \( \ce{CH3F} \) has the highest C-X bond enthalpy.

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol to form a precipitate instantly due to benzylic stabilization?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \) (benzyl chloride) forms a stable benzylic carbocation via \( \ce{S_N1} \), reacting instantly with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form \( \ce{AgCl} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) reacts with excess \( \ce{NH3} \)?

text_solutions: Excess \( \ce{NH3} \) substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \) (propylamine) via \( \ce{S_N2} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{HBr} \) in the presence of benzoyl peroxide?

text_solutions: With peroxide, \( \ce{HBr} \) adds to 2-butene anti-Markovnikov, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromobutane).

qns_content.text: Which compound reacts faster in an \( \ce{S_N2} \) reaction with \( \ce{OH^-} \): \( \ce{CH3Br} \) or \( \ce{CH3I} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{S_N2} \) reactions, the rate depends on the leaving group. Iodide is a better leaving group than bromide due to its larger size and weaker C-X bond, so \( \ce{CH3I} \) reacts faster.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CHOHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \) in pyridine?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SOCl2} \) with pyridine converts 2-butanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHOHCH3} \)) to 2-chlorobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \)) via substitution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest density?

text_solutions: Density increases with molecular weight for similar structures. \( \ce{CH3I} \) (iodomethane) has the highest density among \( \ce{CH3X} \) compounds.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaOCH2CH3} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaOCH2CH3} \) substitutes Cl in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OCH2CH3} \) (ethyl propyl ether).

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts 1-propanol to 1-bromopropane with \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaBr} \) with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) reacts with 1-propanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)) to form 1-bromopropane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \)).

qns_content.text: Which halide has the highest density among the following at room temperature?

text_solutions: Density increases with molecular weight for similar structures. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) (1-iodopropane) has the highest molecular weight.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{KCN} \) in aqueous ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KCN} \) provides \( \ce{CN^-} \), which undergoes nucleophilic substitution with \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CN} \) (propanenitrile).

qns_content.text: Which condition enhances the yield of \( \ce{C6H4Cl2} \) from \( \ce{C6H6} \) with \( \ce{Cl2} \)?

text_solutions: Electrophilic substitution of benzene with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \) in the dark forms \( \ce{C6H4Cl2} \) (1,4-dichlorobenzene) efficiently.

qns_content.text: What is the product of \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) with \( \ce{AgCN} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{AgCN} \) provides \( \ce{NC^-} \) (isocyanide ion), reacting with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2NC} \) (ethyl isocyanide) via nucleophilic substitution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is most reactive towards \( \ce{S_N2} \) substitution with \( \ce{CN^-} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{S_N2} \) favors primary halides due to less steric hindrance. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2I} \) (iodide) is most reactive due to the best leaving group.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain is four carbons (butane), with a methyl group on the second carbon and chlorine on the fourth. The name is 1-chloro-2-methylbutane.

qns_content.text: Which of the following undergoes nucleophilic substitution most readily via \( \ce{S_N1} \) mechanism?

text_solutions: \( \ce{S_N1} \) reactivity increases with carbocation stability. \( \ce{(CH3)3CCl} \) (tertiary) forms a stable tertiary carbocation, making it most reactive.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{PBr3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PBr3} \) converts 1-butanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) to 1-bromobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \)) by replacing \( \ce{OH} \) with Br.

qns_content.text: Which of the following gives a white precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) instantly?

text_solutions: Tertiary halides like \( \ce{(CH3)3CCl} \) ionize readily via \( \ce{S_N1} \), forming \( \ce{AgCl} \) precipitate instantly with \( \ce{AgNO3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH2Br} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) at low temperature?

text_solutions: Elimination (E2) of \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH2Br} \) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) forms \( \ce{(CH3)2C=CHCH3} \) (2-methyl-2-butene) per Zaitsev’s rule.

qns_content.text: What is the order of boiling points of \( \ce{CH3Cl} \), \( \ce{CH3Br} \), and \( \ce{CH3I} \)?

text_solutions: Boiling points increase with molecular weight due to stronger London forces. The order is \( \ce{CH3I} \) (highest) > \( \ce{CH3Br} \) > \( \ce{CH3Cl} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide is a vinylic halide?

text_solutions: A vinylic halide has the halogen on a carbon of a C=C bond. \( \ce{CH3CH=CHBr} \) (1-bromopropene) is vinylic.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a geminal dihalide?

text_solutions: A geminal dihalide has two halogens on the same carbon. \( \ce{CH3CH2CCl2CH3} \) (2,2-dichlorobutane) is geminal.

qns_content.text: Which halide produces a racemic mixture when reacting with \( \ce{OH^-} \) via \( \ce{S_N1} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH3} \) (2-chlorobutane) forms a planar carbocation via \( \ce{S_N1} \), leading to a racemic mixture of 2-butanol.

qns_content.text: Which halide forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2SCH3} \) when reacted with \( \ce{NaSCH3} \) in DMSO?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) undergoes \( \ce{S_N2} \) substitution with \( \ce{NaSCH3} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2SCH3} \) (methyl propyl sulfide).

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{HBr} \) without peroxides?

text_solutions: For 2-pentene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH2CH3} \)), \( \ce{HBr} \) adds via Markovnikov’s rule, forming \( \ce{CH3CHBrCH2CH2CH3} \) (2-bromopentane).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts fastest with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in ethanol tests \( \ce{S_N1} \) reactivity. \( \ce{(CH3)3CBr} \) (tertiary) forms a stable carbocation, reacting fastest.

qns_content.text: How many monochloro isomers are possible for \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)) has three unique carbon positions for Cl substitution (C1/C5, C2/C4, C3), yielding 3 isomers.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{KCN} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KCN} \) substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CN} \) (butanenitrile).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHOHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{PCl5} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PCl5} \) converts 2-pentanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHOHCH3} \)) to 2-chloropentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHClCH3} \)) via substitution.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when toluene reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) in the presence of \( \ce{FeCl3} \)?

text_solutions: Toluene (\( \ce{C6H5CH3} \)) undergoes electrophilic substitution with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \), forming \( \ce{CH3C6H4Cl} \) (chlorotoluene, mainly para).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when aniline reacts with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HBr} \), followed by \( \ce{CuBr} \)?

text_solutions: The Sandmeyer reaction converts aniline to bromobenzene (\( \ce{C6H5Br} \)) via a diazonium salt with \( \ce{CuBr} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzene reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \)?

text_solutions: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \) forms \( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2CH3} \) (propylbenzene).

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to prepare \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) from \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) with \( \ce{ZnCl2} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HCl} \) with \( \ce{ZnCl2} \) (a Lewis acid) converts ethanol to ethyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \)) by facilitating substitution of the \( \ce{OH} \) group.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH2=CH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) in \( \ce{CCl4} \)?

text_solutions: Chlorine adds across the double bond of ethene in a non-polar solvent like \( \ce{CCl4} \), forming 1,2-dichloroethane (\( \ce{CH2ClCH2Cl} \)).

qns_content.text: Which halide forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2NH2} \) when treated with excess \( \ce{NH3} \) followed by heating?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2I} \) reacts with excess \( \ce{NH3} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2NH2} \) (pentylamine) after heating.

qns_content.text: What is the order of bond strength of C-X bonds in \( \ce{CH3F} \), \( \ce{CH3Cl} \), \( \ce{CH3Br} \), and \( \ce{CH3I} \)?

text_solutions: Bond strength decreases as halogen size increases due to weaker overlap: \( \ce{CH3F} \) > \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) > \( \ce{CH3Br} \) > \( \ce{CH3I} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following is prepared by free radical halogenation of an alkane?

text_solutions: Free radical halogenation of propane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \)) with \( \ce{Cl2} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CHClCH3} \) (2-chloropropane) as one product.

qns_content.text: What is the order of reactivity of \( \ce{CH3CH2F} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \), and \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) in \( \ce{S_N2} \) reactions?

text_solutions: \( \ce{S_N2} \) reactivity increases with better leaving group ability: \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) > \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) > \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) > \( \ce{CH3CH2F} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{KOH} \) in methanol?

text_solutions: Alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \) (in methanol) promotes elimination (E2) in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) (propene).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) reacts with sodium in dry ether?

text_solutions: This is a Wurtz reaction, coupling two \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) molecules to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) (hexane).

qns_content.text: How many hydrogen atoms are attached to the carbon bearing chlorine in \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \), the Cl-bearing carbon (C3) is bonded to C2, Cl, C4, and one H, so it has 1 hydrogen.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the reaction between \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) and \( \ce{NaI} \) in dry acetone?

text_solutions: This is a Finkelstein reaction, where an alkyl bromide reacts with \( \ce{NaI} \) in acetone to form the corresponding iodide, \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \), and \( \ce{NaBr} \) precipitates.

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon attached to iodine in \( \ce{CH3CH=CHI} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH=CHI} \), the carbon with I is part of a double bond (C=C), making it sp² hybridized.

qns_content.text: Which halide forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) when treated with \( \ce{Mg} \) in ether followed by \( \ce{H2O} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) forms a Grignard reagent (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2MgBr} \)), which hydrolyzes to pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts 2-propanol to 2-bromopropane?

text_solutions: \( \ce{HBr} \) reacts with 2-propanol (\( \ce{CH3CHOHCH3} \)) to form 2-bromopropane (\( \ce{CH3CHBrCH3} \)) via nucleophilic substitution.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts toluene to \( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \) in the presence of sunlight?

text_solutions: \( \ce{Cl2} \) in sunlight chlorinates the side chain of toluene (\( \ce{C6H5CH3} \)) via free radical substitution to form benzyl chloride (\( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CHOHCH2CH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SOCl2} \) converts 3-pentanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHOHCH2CH3} \)) to 3-chloropentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3} \)) via substitution.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the shortest C-X bond length?

text_solutions: Bond length decreases with smaller halogen size. \( \ce{CH3F} \) has the shortest C-X bond due to fluorine’s small atomic radius.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{HI} \) in the absence of peroxides?

text_solutions: For 1-butene (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \)), \( \ce{HI} \) adds via Markovnikov’s rule, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CHICH3} \) (2-iodobutane).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in dry ether to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) as the sole product?

text_solutions: Wurtz reaction of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) (1-chloropropane) couples to form hexane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: How many carbon atoms are in the longest chain of the compound formed when \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in ether?

text_solutions: Wurtz reaction couples two \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) (2 carbons each) to form butane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)), with a 4-carbon chain.

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzene reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) in the presence of \( \ce{AlCl3} \)?

text_solutions: This is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation. Benzene reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) and \( \ce{AlCl3} \) to form \( \ce{C6H5CH2CH3} \) (ethylbenzene).

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts 1-butanol to 1-chlorobutane with gaseous byproducts?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SOCl2} \) reacts with 1-butanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) to form 1-chlorobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Cl} \)), producing \( \ce{SO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \) gases.

qns_content.text: What happens when \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) is treated with sodium in dry ether?

text_solutions: This is a Wurtz reaction, where two alkyl halides couple to form an alkane. \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \) (butane).

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{HBr} \) in the absence of peroxides?

text_solutions: According to Markovnikov’s rule, \( \ce{HBr} \) adds to propene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \)) such that H attaches to the less substituted carbon, yielding \( \ce{CH3CHBrCH3} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in ether to form a six-carbon alkane with a branched structure?

text_solutions: Wurtz reaction of \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2Cl} \) (1-chloro-2-methylpropane) forms \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2CH2CH(CH3)2} \) (2,5-dimethylhexane), a branched six-carbon alkane.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaSH} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{NaSH} \) substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2I} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2SH} \) (ethanethiol).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{Mg} \) in dry ether, followed by \( \ce{H2O} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \) forms a Grignard reagent with \( \ce{Mg} \), which hydrolyzes with \( \ce{H2O} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \) (butane).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when aniline is treated with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \), followed by \( \ce{CuCl} \)?

text_solutions: This is the Sandmeyer reaction. Aniline forms a diazonium salt with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \), which reacts with \( \ce{CuCl} \) to yield chlorobenzene (\( \ce{C6H5Cl} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound has the IUPAC name 2-bromo-3-methylbutane?

text_solutions: 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane is a four-carbon chain (butane) with Br on C2 and a methyl group on C3: \( \ce{CH3CHBrCH(CH3)CH3} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following forms a yellow precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) slowest?

text_solutions: Primary halides react slowest with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) via \( \ce{S_N1} \). \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) forms \( \ce{AgI} \) (yellow) slowest among the options.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{KSCN} \) in acetone?

text_solutions: \( \ce{KSCN} \) provides \( \ce{SCN^-} \), which substitutes Br in \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) to form \( \ce{CH3CH2SCN} \) (ethyl thiocyanate) via \( \ce{S_N2} \).

qns_content.text: What is the C-X bond length order for \( \ce{CH3F} \), \( \ce{CH3Cl} \), \( \ce{CH3Br} \), and \( \ce{CH3I} \)?

text_solutions: C-X bond length increases with halogen size: \( \ce{CH3F} \) < \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) < \( \ce{CH3Br} \) < \( \ce{CH3I} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide undergoes \( \ce{S_N1} \) substitution with \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form a racemic mixture of alcohols?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \) (2-chlorobutane) forms a planar secondary carbocation via \( \ce{S_N1} \), yielding a racemic mixture of 2-butanol.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \) without gaseous byproducts?

text_solutions: \( \ce{PCl5} \) reacts with 2-butanol to form 2-chlorobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHClCH3} \)) with \( \ce{POCl3} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \), but \( \ce{HCl} \) can be trapped, avoiding gaseous release.

qns_content.text: Which halogen has the highest electronegativity in alkyl halides?

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down the halogen group. Fluorine, being at the top, has the highest electronegativity among F, Cl, Br, and I.

qns_content.text: Which of the following can be prepared by reacting an alkene with \( \ce{HI} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2I} \) (1-iodobutane) can be prepared by adding \( \ce{HI} \) to 1-butene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \)) under anti-Markovnikov conditions with peroxides.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{HBr} \) in the presence of \( \ce{C6H5COOOH} \)?

text_solutions: With peroxide (\( \ce{C6H5COOOH} \)), \( \ce{HBr} \) adds to propene anti-Markovnikov, forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromopropane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{AgCN} \) in ethanol?

text_solutions: \( \ce{AgCN} \) substitutes Br with \( \ce{NC^-} \) (isocyanide form) via \( \ce{S_N1} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NC} \) (propyl isocyanide).

qns_content.text: What is the product when toluene reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in the presence of \( \ce{FeBr3} \)?

text_solutions: Toluene (\( \ce{C6H5CH3} \)) undergoes electrophilic substitution with \( \ce{Br2} \) and \( \ce{FeBr3} \), forming \( \ce{CH3C6H4Br} \) (bromotoluene, mainly para).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{HCl} \)?

text_solutions: For 2-butene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \)), \( \ce{HCl} \) adds via Markovnikov’s rule, forming \( \ce{CH3CHClCH2CH3} \) (2-chlorobutane) as the major product.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) in dry ether?

text_solutions: This is a Wurtz reaction, coupling two \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) molecules to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) (octane).

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in water?

text_solutions: Aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \) provides \( \ce{OH^-} \), which substitutes I in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2I} \) via \( \ce{S_N2} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \) (1-propanol).

qns_content.text: Which of the following does not undergo nucleophilic substitution easily?

text_solutions: Aryl halides like \( \ce{C6H5Cl} \) have a strong C-Cl bond due to resonance, making them resistant to nucleophilic substitution under normal conditions.

qns_content.text: Which halide has the carbon-halogen bond most susceptible to nucleophilic attack due to steric hindrance?

text_solutions: \( \ce{(CH3)3CCH2CH2Cl} \) (primary) has less steric hindrance than tertiary halides, but among the options, its C-Cl bond is most accessible for \( \ce{S_N2} \).

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) to \( \ce{C6H5Cl} \) via a diazonium intermediate?

text_solutions: The Sandmeyer reaction uses \( \ce{CuCl} \) with \( \ce{NaNO2} \) and \( \ce{HCl} \) to convert aniline to chlorobenzene via a diazonium salt.

qns_content.text: What is the product when \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \) reacts with \( \ce{SOCl2} \)?

text_solutions: Reaction of a primary alcohol like 1-propanol with \( \ce{SOCl2} \) replaces the \( \ce{OH} \) group with \( \ce{Cl} \), forming \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) (1-chloropropane).

qns_content.text: What is the order of boiling points of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2F} \), \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \), and \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \)?

text_solutions: Boiling point increases with molecular weight: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2F} \) < \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) < \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Br} \).

qns_content.text: Which halide reacts fastest with \( \ce{NaOH} \) in water due to resonance stabilization of the carbocation?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C6H5CH2CH2Cl} \) forms a benzylic carbocation stabilized by resonance, reacting fastest via \( \ce{S_N1} \) with \( \ce{NaOH} \).

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to convert an alkyl chloride to an alkyl fluoride?

text_solutions: The Swarts reaction uses a metallic fluoride like \( \ce{AgF} \) to convert an alkyl chloride or bromide to an alkyl fluoride.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a vinylic halide?

text_solutions: A vinylic halide has the halogen directly attached to a carbon in a C=C bond. \( \ce{CH2=CHCl} \) (vinyl chloride) is a vinylic halide.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when \( \ce{(CH3)3CBr} \) reacts with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Tertiary alkyl halides like \( \ce{(CH3)3CBr} \) undergo elimination (E2) with alcoholic \( \ce{KOH} \), forming the alkene \( \ce{(CH3)2C=CH2} \) (2-methylpropene).

qns_content.text: Which of the following gives a precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) fastest?

text_solutions: Tertiary halides ionize fastest via \( \ce{S_N1} \). \( \ce{(CH3)2CHC(CH3)2I} \) (iodide) forms a precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) most rapidly.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH2Cl)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain is three carbons (propane), with a chloromethyl group on the second carbon. The name is 1-chloro-2-methylpropane.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when ethylbenzene reacts with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \)?

text_solutions: Ethylbenzene (\( \ce{C6H5CH2CH3} \)) undergoes electrophilic substitution with \( \ce{Cl2} \) and \( \ce{FeCl3} \), forming \( \ce{C6H4(CH2CH3)Cl} \) (chloroethylbenzene, mainly para).

qns_content.text: Which of the following can be prepared by reacting an alkene with \( \ce{HBr} \) in the presence of peroxides?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Br} \) (1-bromobutane) is formed by anti-Markovnikov addition of \( \ce{HBr} \) to 1-butene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \)) with peroxides.
